chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
And he struck with his hand toward cushions in the house: cushions upon which the Angels had long leaned, and sometimes we would pick up some of their fluff.

key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the Angels, described here as visiting and leaning upon the furnishings
key_terms.زَغَبِهَا: their fluff or fine down, understood here as from the Angels
key_terms.مَسَاوِرُ: cushions or bolsters in the house

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the presence of the Angels with the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the nearness of the mala'ikah to the Imam عليه السلام and their presence in his household. It indicates a special unseen connection and honor granted to the Imam, such that even the furnishings of the house are touched by the mala'ikah.
